Foote et al. 2025, Nature Genetics. Genomic SEM over frailty-index deficits: a general frailty factor and six
residual factors, one of them "multimorbidity" (factor 3). Inputs are consortium GWAS where available, otherwise the
Pan-UK Biobank's summary statistics, so its sample overlaps UK Biobank (Zenin 2019's). Europe PMC's open full text is
read; the per-locus tables are not, but the factor 3 deposit is (row 51).

## Reading 2026-11-11, full_text

> [q1] the multimorbidity factor (defined by the number of illnesses and high mean arterial pressure) is a strong driver of frailty over and above the variance captured by a general aggregate measure of all frailty deficits

> [q2] The effect estimates for each trait were formatted in a direction that reflected the ‘risk-inducing’ phenotype for frailty

> [q3] When consortia data were not available, we used GWAS summary statistics downloaded from the Pan-UK Biobank

Factor 3 is defined in part by high mean arterial pressure (q1), and effects point to the frailty-raising side (q2):
a negative β is less frailty. Its set at 4p14 (Open Targets, db-opentargets-26.09#q422-q425) colocalises with the
blood-pressure sets at H4 about 0.98, so at row 27 it is read as the blood-pressure signal carried into a frailty
factor, supporting healthspan but not separate evidence of it. UK Biobank enters through the Pan-UK Biobank inputs
(q3). For row 27.

## Reading 2026-11-11, supplement

> [q4] Multivariate GWAS summary statistics for Factor 3 in the latent model

> [q5] represent frailty pathways shared between frailty deficits linked to Multimorbidity

> [q6] 7	129685597	G	A	0.0144044878093618	0.00173162624511149	0.614314	8.91030786590252e-17	rs56179563	699030	11.6418317027102	0.000644850728367752

The deposit for factor 3 (GCST90624049, GWAS-SSF; `GCST90624049-meta.yaml`, `rows-d17a51cd`, GRCh37): the authors
call it multivariate GWAS summary statistics (q4), for the pathways shared by the deficits linked to multimorbidity
(q5); analysis software Genomic SEM, the method of Rosoff 2023's mvAge; n is the factor's expected N (Nhat). At
rs56179563 (q6): G (0.61) raises the frailty factor, β +0.0144 (SE 0.0017), P 8.9 × 10⁻¹⁷, n 699,030; the Q
heterogeneity index 11.6, P 6.4 × 10⁻⁴, under the deposit's filter (7.14 × 10⁻⁹), so kept, though the SNP fits the
factor imperfectly. Effects point to the frailty-raising side (q2), so A, Timmers' lifespan-raising allele, is the
less frail one. The set colocalises with coronary disease and blood pressure (db-opentargets-26.09#q654, q655), so,
as at row 27, the factor carries the cardiovascular signal. For row 51.

## Reading 2026-11-12, supplement

Row 59 (ABO, rs2519093, GRCh37 9:136,141,870): the general factor's and factors 2, 3 and 4's deposits (GCST90624046,
48, 49, 50; `rows-87539b85`, GRCh37 9:136.05 to 136.24 Mb) returned no row in the window. Factor 3's file is byte for
byte the one read at row 51 (its sha256), so for factor 3 the region is absent from the deposit, not lost in the fetch,
likely removed by its Q filter; the other three files' completeness was not checked. Factors 1, 5 and 6 (47, 51, 52)
hold 495 SNPs there but not the lead or any r² >= 0.8 proxy; their smallest P are 0.005, 8e-4 and 0.009. Open Targets
holds no Foote set within 3 Mb of ABO (db-opentargets-26.09#q746; all 426 sets read, the nearest 3.4 Mb away). So
Foote at the lead is unknown, neither tested nor flat, and gives row 59 no multivariate anchor; the row is B on
Timmers' own Bayesian call instead (D28.7). No quote: an absence.
